headline: Greg Canavan warns Wesfarmers is aggressively priced at 30x earnings with limited internal compounding and rising profit-warning risk
reasoning: Canavan acknowledges Wesfarmers is a quality business with quality assets, but argues it is priced very aggressively at 30 times earnings with a dividend payout ratio of 90%, meaning very little is being reinvested to generate internal compounding. With a sub-3% dividend yield, he sees no growth-asset justification for the valuation. He believes the elevated price reflects super funds treating it as a safe harbour, but warns that if the economy continues to slow and cost pressures build, the risk of a profit warning rises materially — and highly priced companies have seen significant share price falls when they warn, as seen with CSL and Cochlear.
quote: The issue I have with a company like Wesfarmers is it is priced, um, very, very aggressively. So it trades on 30 times earnings, it distributes its got a dividend payout ratio of 90%. So it's not really reinvesting much back into the business and you're not getting a lot of internal compounding. So therefore you can't really look at it as a growth asset. Yet it is priced at 30 times earnings. Dividend yield of under 3%. To me, you're paying a very, very high price for yes, what is a quality asset... when you're trading on 30 times earnings, you can't really afford to put a foot wrong. And if the economy is continuing to slow, if their cost pressures are continuing, continuing to build, I see that as an increasing risk for a business like that.

headline: Greg Canavan sees the US semiconductor bubble beginning to burst after parabolic moves, with volatility and further downside likely
reasoning: Canavan notes that stocks like SK Hynix have made parabolic moves over recent months, and such moves rarely unwind in an orderly manner. The semiconductor index fell 10% on Friday before a 5% bounce Monday, which he characterises as typical bull-bear arm-wrestling at the start of a bubble burst. He believes this marks the beginning of the end for the extraordinary run in the semiconductor space.
quote: If you look at some of the charts of those companies that have really run strongly over the past couple of months, and particularly companies like SK Hynix, uh, the memory chip stocks, they have effectively been parabolic moves over the past couple of couple of months, and when you tend to get those moves, they tend not to be unwound in an orderly manner. There is a panic on the way in and panic on the way out. So my view is that the the bubble in that particular sector has started to burst. And you saw a 10% fall in the semiconductor index on Friday.
